old: Every tracker read returns a **resident** block, re-billed as `cache_read` every later turn — so a read's cost is `size × turns-resident`, and the cheapest lever is not fetching what the step won't read. Orthogonal to **Always pull fresh** (that rule is *when* you read; this is *how much*) — a lean read is still a fresh read. Single-homed here so call sites reference it, exactly as they reference **Always pull fresh**. It shrinks what a call *returns* but cannot evict an already-resident body — same-agent prose can't delete a received tool_result, so eviction is a separate lever (subagent isolation / an out-of-context CLI). When the id is already known, prefer a single `get_issue` to a `list_issues` — one targeted object beats a filtered sweep.
new: Tracker responses remain in context, costing `size × turns-resident` as later `cache_read`s. Fetch only what the step consumes while obeying **Always pull fresh**. Call sites reference this shared rule. Lean reads reduce returned data but cannot evict prior tool results; eviction requires subagent isolation or an out-of-context CLI. With a known id, prefer one `get_issue` over `list_issues`.
reason: Remove repeated cost explanation; preserve fresh-read complement, eviction limit and targeted-read preference.

old: **Comments are not optional.** Because faff-prep writes specs to comments by default, any spec-discovery pass that only inspects descriptions is **invalid output** — it will systematically miss the most common case and produce false "no spec" findings. Before classifying any issue as "no spec / almost ready / needs prep", you **must** fetch its comments via whichever tracker MCP is configured (use the tracker's list-comments tool — autodetect from the available MCP, don't hardcode). Sampling descriptions and noting "comments not checked" is **not** acceptable — re-fetch and complete the check before reporting.
new: **Comments are not optional.** Specs are stored in comments by default, so description-only spec discovery is invalid. Before reporting "no spec / almost ready / needs prep", fetch comments through the configured tracker's list-comments tool, autodetected from available MCP rather than hardcoded. "Comments not checked" is unacceptable: re-fetch and finish before reporting.
reason: Remove repeated false-finding rationale; preserve mandatory tool discovery/fetch and refusal to report incomplete checks.

old: **A description is never a spec — no exceptions.** However clear, detailed, or well-defined a ticket's description is, it does not satisfy the spec gate and must be formalised into a spec via `/faff-prep` before any build. No faff sub-skill may offer to build straight from a description, skip prep because "the description is already clear," or treat well-defined requirements as a substitute for the spec. Well-defined is a reason prep will be *fast*, not a reason to skip it. The spec is the durable, reviewable artefact the build is gated on; the description is not.
new: **A description is never a spec — no exceptions.** Before any build, formalise even clear, detailed requirements through `/faff-prep` into a durable reviewable spec. No sub-skill may offer a direct description-to-build path or skip prep because the requirements are clear.

old: Sibling of the **Chaining pattern**: that gates *decisions*; this governs *continuation and offers* at phase boundaries and stops.
